description.narrative: The Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Small-Scale Irrigation, a project of the U.S. Governments Feed the Future Initiative, is a five-year project in Ethiopia, Ghana and Tanzania aimed at benefiting the regions farmers by improving effective use of scarce water supplies through interventions in small-scale irrigation. The project, led by the Norman Borlaug Institute for International Agriculture at Texas A&M University and funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID,) intends to develop management protocols and practices to reduce poverty and improve nutrition.
pour soutenir le laboratoire d'innovation Feed the Furture pour la recherche collaborative sur le sorgho et le mil.

Le laboratoire d'innovation Feed the Future pour l'irrigation à petite échelle, un projet du gouvernement américain Feed the Future Initiative, est un projet quinquennal en Éthiopie, au Ghana et en Tanzanie visant à bénéficier aux agriculteurs de la région en améliorant l'utilisation efficace des rares réserves d'eau grâce à des interventions dans l'irrigation à petite échelle. Le projet, dirigé par l'Institut Norman Borlaug pour l'agriculture internationale de la Texas A&M University et financé par l'Agence américaine pour le développement international (USAID), vise à développer des protocoles et des pratiques de gestion pour réduire la pauvreté et améliorer la nutrition.

title.narrative: Delivering Contraceptive Vaginal Rings Project

description.narrative: This project will further the development and introduction of two new womaninitiated contraceptive methods by: Completing the development and regulatory approval of the one- year Nesterone(TM)/Ethinyl-Estradiol (NES/EE) contraceptive vaginal ring (CVR), and initiating its introduction into priority countries; Expanding availability in developing country markets of the three-month Progesterone Vaginal Ring (PVR) for postpartum women who are breastfeeding The NES/EE CVR and PVR will be piloted for introduction through both the public and private sectors, including through social marketing and not-for-profit providers, with the potential of reaching up to twenty-five million users. Introduction strategies will focus on provision through multiple channels, including commercial outlets and community outreach initiatives. To complete this work, the Population Council will collaborate with donors and agencies involved in obtaining regulatory approvals and prequalification, as well as procurement organizations to facilitate the process of introduction.

title.narrative: EVIDENCE Project
Projet EVIDENCE
Projet EVIDENCE

description.narrative: The Evidence Project uses implementation science - the strategic generation, translation, and use of evidence - to improve family planning policies, programs, and practices. The project is led by the Population Council. Over the course of the project (2013-2020), the Evidence Project was implemented in partnership with INDEPTH Network, International Planned Parenthood Federation, PATH, Population Reference Bureau, Meridian Group International, Management Sciences for Health, and the projects University Resource Network. The Evidence Project is investigating which strategies work best in improving, expanding, and sustaining family planning services. It is also evaluating how to implement and scale up those strategies. Critical to the Evidence Project is translating this knowledge and working with stakeholders to apply the evidence and to build capacity in using implementation science to improve policies, programs, and practices.

Faisant suite au projet initial Africa Lead, Africa Lead II renforce les capacités de la hiérarchie agricole africaine à développer, gérer et diriger des programmes. L'Evidence Project utilise la science de la mise en œuvre - la génération stratégique, la traduction et l'utilisation de preuves - pour améliorer les politiques, programmes et pratiques de planification familiale. Le projet est dirigé par le Conseil de la population. Au cours du projet (2013-2020), le projet Evidence a été mis en œuvre en partenariat avec le réseau INDEPTH, la Fédération internationale pour la planification familiale, PATH, le Population Reference Bureau, Meridian Group International, Management Sciences for Health et le projet University Resource Network. L'Evidence Project étudie quelles stratégies fonctionnent le mieux pour améliorer, étendre et maintenir les services de planification familiale. Il évalue également comment mettre en œuvre et intensifier ces stratégies. Il est essentiel pour le projet Evidence de traduire ces connaissances et de travailler avec les parties prenantes pour appliquer les preuves et renforcer les capacités d'utilisation de la science de la mise en œuvre pour améliorer les politiques, les programmes et les pratiques.

title.narrative: Expanding Effective Contraceptive Options (EECO)

description.narrative: Over 100 million women cite method-related reasons for non-use of modern contraceptives, underscoring the need for new and improved contraceptive methods and greater method choice. The EECO project is designed to support the research, development and introduction of technologies that meet the full range of sexual and reproductive health needs of women and girls. The EECO teams objective is to produce roadmaps for introducing and creating demand for new woman-initiated family planning methods, including vaginal gels, barrier methods, and intra-vaginal rings. EECO will produce actionable information on how best to register products, which distribution and communication channels have the most traction, what kind of training and advocacy is required, and how to segment the market for each method. These results can then be extrapolated to bring products to national scale, helping to fill critical gaps in the family planning method mix.

title.narrative: ARP- FTFIL for Climate Resilient Chickpea (UC Davis)

description.narrative: The Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Climate Resilient Chickpea (Chickpea IL) aims to harness the genetic diversity of wild chickpea species to improve the yield, climate resilience, nutritional value, and nitrogen-fixing properties of chickpea varieties grown by smallholder farmers. Researchers will combine advanced genomic technologies with analysis of plant traits to identify new and desirable genes harbored by chickpea's closest wild relatives, and partner with Ethiopian breeding programs to introduce these novel genes into chickpea varieties selected in consultation with local farmers.

title.narrative: Completion of Phase III Microbicide Clinical Trial for Tenofovir 1% Gel

description.narrative: The objectives of this program are to complete clinical and regulatory activities required for licensure of tenofovir (TFV) 1% gel for the prevention of vaginal HIV acquisition in women and to provide information about its implementation in African populations. This project includes the following activities: 1) Completing clinical activities required for TFV 1% gel licensure; 2) Completing regulatory activities required for TFV 1% gel licensure; 3) Conducting open-label TFV 1% gel Implementation Studies in South Africa and other African countries; 4) Conducting a bridging study for the approval of one TFV 1% gel that is safe and acceptable for vaginal and rectal use.

title.narrative: Maternal and Child Survival Program (MCSP - formerly RMNCH)
Programme de survie de la mère et de l'enfant (MCSP - anciennement RMNCH)

description.narrative: The United States Agency for International Developments (USAID) Bureau for Global Healths flagship Maternal and Child Survival Program (MCSP) focuses on 25 high-priority countries with the ultimate goal of preventing child and maternal deaths. The Program is introducing and supporting high-impact, sustainable reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health (RMNCH) interventions in partnership with ministries of health and other partners. MCSP places a greater emphasis on key cross-cutting issues such as innovation, e/mHealth, equity, quality, gender, public-private partnerships and involvement of civil society, community approaches, health systems strengthening, and behavior change interventions. While maintaining a focus on technical, high-impact interventions; the Program works toward sustainable scale-up to include the health systems that deliver these interventions. In addition to contributing to high-level technical and policy dialogue at the global level, the Program provides tailored technical assistance to help countries meet specific priorities and contextual needs of local RMNCH programs.

Le programme phare de survie de la mère et de l'enfant (MCSP) du Bureau de la santé mondiale de l'Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) se concentre sur 25 pays hautement prioritaires dans le but ultime de prévenir les décès d'enfants et de mères. Le programme introduit et soutient des interventions durables et à fort impact en matière de santé reproductive, maternelle, néonatale et infantile (SRMNI), en partenariat avec les ministères de la Santé et d'autres partenaires. Le MCSP met davantage l'accent sur des questions transversales clés telles que l'innovation, l'e/mSanté, l'équité, la qualité, le genre, les partenariats public-privé et l'implication de la société civile, les approches communautaires, le renforcement des systèmes de santé et les interventions de changement de comportement. Tout en restant concentré sur les interventions techniques à fort impact ; le programme œuvre à une intensification durable pour inclure les systèmes de santé qui fournissent ces interventions. En plus de contribuer au dialogue technique et politique de haut niveau au niveau mondial, le programme fournit une assistance technique sur mesure pour aider les pays à répondre aux priorités spécifiques et aux besoins contextuels des programmes locaux de RMNCH.

El Programa emblemático de Supervivencia Materna e Infantil (MCSP) de la Oficina de Salud Global de la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional (USAID) se centra en 25 países de alta prioridad con el objetivo final de prevenir las muertes infantiles y maternas. El Programa está introduciendo y apoyando intervenciones sostenibles y de alto impacto en materia de salud reproductiva, materna, neonatal e infantil (RMNCH) en asociación con ministerios de salud y otros socios. MCSP pone un mayor énfasis en cuestiones transversales clave como la innovación, la e/mSalud, la equidad, la calidad, el género, las asociaciones público-privadas y la participación de la sociedad civil, los enfoques comunitarios, el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de salud y las intervenciones de cambio de comportamiento. Manteniendo al mismo tiempo un enfoque en intervenciones técnicas de alto impacto; El Programa trabaja para lograr una ampliación sostenible para incluir los sistemas de salud que realizan estas intervenciones. Además de contribuir al diálogo técnico y político de alto nivel a nivel mundial, el Programa proporciona asistencia técnica personalizada para ayudar a los países a satisfacer prioridades específicas y necesidades contextuales de los programas locales de RMNCH.

O principal Programa de Sobrevivência Materna e Infantil (MCSP) do Bureau para Saúde Global da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID) concentra-se em 25 países de alta prioridade com o objetivo final de prevenir mortes infantis e maternas. O Programa está a introduzir e a apoiar intervenções de alto impacto e sustentáveis ​​de saúde reprodutiva, materna, neonatal e infantil (SRMNI) em parceria com ministérios da saúde e outros parceiros. O MCSP dá maior ênfase às principais questões transversais, como inovação, e/mHealth, equidade, qualidade, género, parcerias público-privadas e envolvimento da sociedade civil, abordagens comunitárias, reforço dos sistemas de saúde e intervenções de mudança de comportamento. Mantendo o foco em intervenções técnicas de alto impacto; o Programa trabalha no sentido de uma expansão sustentável para incluir os sistemas de saúde que realizam estas intervenções. Além de contribuir para o diálogo técnico e político de alto nível a nível global, o Programa fornece assistência técnica personalizada para ajudar os países a satisfazer prioridades específicas e necessidades contextuais dos programas locais de SRMNI.

The initiative will contribute to the strategic goal of protecting democratic space, and increasing the capacity of independent civil society groups. The program supports focus on two areas.
